    By Staff Report
    PUBLISHED: August 31, 2026 at 8:45 PM EDT
    Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...

    Chrysanthemum sale at Griggs Farm

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 3:45
    Instaread

    BILLERICA — The Griggs Farm mums sale runs through Monday, Sept. 7, 599 Boston Road. Griggs Farm has been family-owned and operated since 1943, with 52 acres of preserved farmland and 14 greenhouses. It is open daily from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. For more information, call 978-667-9111.

    Habitat for Humanity Gala

    CONCORD — Habitat for Humanity of Greater Lowell hosts its 19th annual Dream Builders Gala on Friday, Sept. 18, from 6 to 10 p.m., at Nashawtuc Country Club, 1861 Sudbury Road.

    This signature fundraising event aims to raise over $150,000 in support of affordable housing initiatives across 16 towns in Greater Lowell. Guests will enjoy a formal evening featuring a seated dinner, music, and silent and live auctions. Funds raised will directly support Habitat’s mission to build, rehabilitate and repair safe, affordable homes for low-income families in the region.

    “Our community is facing a real housing crisis,” Executive Director Sheilagh Carlisle said. “This Gala isn’t just a night out — it’s a way to come together and do something meaningful. Every ticket, every donation helps a local family build a stable home and a better future. When we invest in our neighbors, we strengthen the entire community.”

    Habitat for Humanity of Greater Lowell has expanded its building efforts from one home per year to four, with projects underway in Westford and Concord. In Concord. Habitat builds and rehabilitates safe, affordable housing and provides critical home repairs to help low-income families, seniors, and veterans remain safe in their homes. Since 1991, Habitat Greater Lowell has helped more than 53 families achieve stability and self-reliance through homeownership.

    Tickets and sponsorship opportunities are available at lowellhabitat.org/gala.

    Save the date: Sharps and medication disposal day

    LOWELL — The city Health Department is sponsoring an unwanted medication and sharps disposal day on Saturday, Sept. 19, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at the Senior Center, located at 276 Broadway St. Prescription and over-the-counter medications are accepted, as are inhalers, EpiPens, nasal sprays, lancets and Narcan. All pill medications must be in plastic bags — no bottles — and sharps must be in a puncture-proof container. Residential disposal only, no commercial disposal. For information, call 978-674-4304 or visit lowellma.gov.

    Call the Lowell Health Department for any discarded needles found in parks, fields or other public areas. To have those syringes removed, call 978-674-1049. On nights and weekends, call the nonemergency police phone line at 978-937-3200.

    The LHD and the city of Lowell provide various ways to properly dispose of sharps, including needles, lancets, EpiPens and syringes. Sharps should never be thrown loosely into the trash, recycling or toilet as they are a safety risk to the public and sanitation workers. Sharps that retract after use, or are very small, should be disposed of like all other sharps. For a list of safe disposal locations call 978-674-4304 or visit bit.ly/4cmqiaO.

    Mark your calendars: Walking tours of Lowell cemetery

    LOWELL — Walk through Lowell Cemetery and learn about the history, monuments and lives of those buried there during walking tours led by Lowell Cemetery Trustee and former Middlesex North Register of Deeds Richard Howe on Saturday,Sept. 26, and again on Sunday, Sept. 27, both at 10 a.m.

    According to a statement Howe posted to his website, “Lowell Cemetery was founded in 1842 as one of New England’s earliest garden-style cemeteries. It covers 88 acres of landscape terrain along the Concord River.”

    Both tours begin inside the Lawrence Street entrance. Parking is available within the cemetery. The 90-minute tours will be held rain or shine (but not in thunderstorms or severe downpours), are free and require no advance registration, but include a moderate amount of walking.

    For more information, visit lowellcemetery.com.
